speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with gait and limb ataxia and a significant medical history; to begin our assessment, have you noticed any progressive weakness, numbness, or changes in your vision or balance over the past few months?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of appearing "drunk" and feeling clumsy, particularly on the right side, suggest a focal neurological issue. To better understand the progression and underlying cause, can you describe your significant medical history in detail? Also, have you experienced any specific visual disturbances, such as double vision or loss of vision in one eye?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy.

The combination of subacute ataxia, hemispatial clumsiness (right-sided), and a history of natalizumab use for Crohn's disease is highly suspicious for PML. Given the specificity of this risk, we need to confirm the diagnosis immediately.
REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with and without contrast.
REQUEST IMAGES: Axial T2-weighted MRI of the brain to look for non-enhancing white matter lesions.
